subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: How should Mattermost interaction signing secrets be provisioned so forged bot-token-derived callbacks are rejected while valid callbacks still work across restarts and split processes?
rationale: The source-level vulnerability is clear, but the fix changes a channel security boundary and credential/setup behavior that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Require durable credential provisioning
options.body: Make the signing secret configured or persisted through supported setup, SecretRef, docs, and upgrade-test surfaces before merging a fix.

options.title: Accept explicit fail-closed setup
options.body: Require operators to configure an interaction secret and make the missing-secret failure mode clear in code, docs, and tests.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow replacement
options.body: Pause the current dirty candidate branch and land a maintainer-owned replacement once the credential model is chosen.

recommendation.title: Require durable credential provisioning
recommendation.body: Make the signing secret configured or persisted through supported setup, SecretRef, docs, and upgrade-test surfaces before merging a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Mattermost callback hardening and release provenance make this the strongest available security-boundary routing signal from current history.
